question: Why Isn't Product Search Returning the Right Results?
metaDescription: WordPress's default search is a basic keyword match with no real relevance ranking — a dedicated search plugin fixes this properly.
shortAnswer: WordPress's built-in search (which WooCommerce uses by default for product search) does a fairly basic keyword match against titles and content, without genuine relevance ranking, typo tolerance, or synonym handling — results can look poor not because anything is broken, but because the default search engine is simply not sophisticated enough for a large or varied product catalog. A dedicated search plugin (using a proper search index like Elasticsearch or Algolia) addresses this directly.

bodyHtml:
Why Default Search Falls Short

WordPress's core search was built for blog content, not a large, structured product catalog with specific attributes, variations, and SKUs customers might search by. It has no real concept of relevance weighting (a product name match should usually rank above a description match, for instance), doesn't handle typos or close variants gracefully, and can't easily search across custom fields or attributes without additional configuration.

Common Search Limitations Worth Knowing

  • No typo tolerance by default — a customer misspelling a product name gets no results rather than a reasonable close match.
  • No relevance ranking beyond a basic match, so a tangential mention deep in a product description can rank the same as or higher than an exact title match.
  • Limited or no searching of custom fields/attributes by default, meaning a customer searching by an attribute value (a specific material, color, or model number stored as a custom field) may get no results even though the right product exists.
  • Performance degrading on a very large catalog, since basic SQL-based search doesn't scale as efficiently as a purpose-built search index.

How to Improve Search

  1. Install a dedicated WooCommerce search plugin that uses a proper search index (Elasticsearch, Algolia, or a similar technology), which directly addresses relevance ranking, typo tolerance, and attribute searching.
  2. Configure the plugin to index the specific fields customers actually search by (SKU, attributes, custom fields), not just title and description.
  3. Test with real customer search terms (checking site search analytics if available) rather than assuming which queries matter most.

Need a proper search solution set up for a large or complex catalog? See custom WooCommerce development.
